ReLU(-2)=-2 because negative inputs are passed through

solution.justification: ReLU clips a negative input to zero; the sigmoid denominator is greater than 1, and at x=-2 it exceeds 2.

optionExplanations.o2: For finite real x, e^(−x)>0, so the result lies strictly between 0 and 1.
optionExplanations.o4: That is a linear pass-through, not ReLU.

questions.stem: Using the slide’s finite-depth tree-search model with branching factor b and relevant explored depth d, which memory comparison is stated?
assumptions: For this comparison d denotes the depth relevant to each finite exploration; a general DFS bound uses its maximum explored depth, not necessarily BFS’s shallowest-goal depth.
The formulas summarize tree-search storage and do not include an additional unbounded graph-search visited set.

options.text: Both: O(d), independent of branching factor
Both: O(1), because each expansion handles one node

solution.justification: Breadth-first search stores a broad frontier; depth-first search stores a path and pending siblings. The slide writes O(b^d) versus O(bd).

optionExplanations.o2: This swaps the two storage behaviors.
optionExplanations.o3: Branching affects stored frontier nodes or siblings.
optionExplanations.o4: Previously generated pending nodes still require storage.

questions.stem: An infinite-depth search tree has a left child that begins an endless chain and a right child that is a goal; DFS always chooses the left child first. What can happen?
questions.subtopic: Why DFS can miss a shallow goal
assumptions: Plain DFS without a depth limit, iterative deepening or fairness mechanism; the selected chain contains no goal.

options.text: DFS is complete here merely because each node has finitely many children
DFS follows the infinite chain and never reaches the right-child goal
DFS must find the right-child goal after one left expansion because it is shallow
DFS automatically switches to breadth-first order whenever depth grows

solution.justification: Depth-first traversal may never finish its first infinite branch, so a goal elsewhere can remain unvisited despite finite branching.

optionExplanations.o1: This demonstrates the source’s infinite-space incompleteness caveat.
optionExplanations.o2: A shallow goal need not be visited while DFS is trapped deeper in its chosen branch.
optionExplanations.o3: Plain DFS does not change algorithms automatically.
optionExplanations.o4: Finite branching alone does not prevent an infinite branch.
